summary.headline: Strides Q1 FY27 revenue grew 13% YoY with EBITDA margin at 18.2%, while US revenue was flat at ₹6,282m and Ex-US grew 17% to ₹5,875m.
summary.overview: Strides reported 13% YoY topline growth and 5.4% YoY EBITDA growth to ₹229.8 crore at an 18.2% margin, absorbing about ₹13.1 crore of geopolitical freight and operating costs. Reported PAT rose 56.7% to ₹165.5 crore, helped by a ₹53.4 crore net gain from divesting majority stake in Pivot Path. Ex-US revenue grew 17% YoY but fell sequentially from $70m in Q4 FY26 to $63m on supply-chain shipment delays that management calls timing, not demand. US revenue was flat at ₹6,282m ($68m) amid competition in newer launches, and management guided that H2 FY27 will be stronger.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹6,282m ($68m), stable despite competition in recently launched products; 72 commercialised products, 2 launched in the quarter; top-3 positions in 37 products contributing ~70% of US revenue. Chestnut Ridge (US) supplies nearly one-third of US revenue.

segments.name: Ex-US
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹5,875m ($63m), +17% YoY but down from $70m in Q4 FY26 due to supply-chain shipment delays; management expects ~$7m spillover to be recovered in coming quarters. Africa grew strongly via Brands business; UK prescription and Europe/Nordic Branded and OTC performed well.

segments.name: Pivot Path (GCC)
segments.commentary: Majority stake divested, generating ₹74.2 crore gross gain (₹53.4 crore net of tax); Strides retains 20% stake per analyst question.

guidance_outlook: US revenue growth expected to improve in H2 FY27 on new approvals and launches; first two quarters described as soft.
About 10 product launches targeted from now until 31 March 2027.

Ambition of $375m North America business by FY28 retained; management says ~$80-90m must be added from levers including OTC, controlled substances, 100-plus unlaunched products, specialty channels and partnerships.
Ex-US expected to grow faster than company average; Sandoz acquisition expected to close in Q2 FY27 (subject to permissions) and contribute from H2.
Gross margin to stay within 58-60% range; objective of superior EBITDA margins over medium term.
Capex of ₹2.5-3.0 billion per year (maintenance, R&D and hard capex); no greenfield plans at present.
Net debt-neutral targeted in 2-3 years, per management.
capex_capacity: Annual capex envelope ₹2.5-3.0 billion covering maintenance capex, R&D and hard capex, focused on existing factories and high-impact line items.
No greenfield capex being considered currently.
Chestnut Ridge, US facility supplies about one-third of US revenue; controlled substances, nasal sprays, transdermal patches and films are being built around this platform.

Bengaluru plant received a USFDA inspection in May 2026 with observations; response submitted, and management expects USFDA feedback by end-August or September 2026; no current supply impact anticipated.
demand_pricing: US: increased competition in certain products launched over the last few quarters; management says growth strategy prioritises profitability over volume.

US controlled substances: about 5% of group revenue; 4 products demonstrated over ~20 months; quota allocations occur twice yearly (June and December); June-cycle outcome not yet received, December response expected.

Nasal spray: first filing in advanced review, approval expected in H2 FY27 (Q3/Q4 timeframe); second filed about a month ago with 12-15 month review; 5-6 nasal spray programmes planned, plus transdermal and film programmes.
Proposed US tariffs on generic pharmaceuticals from August 2028 flagged; implementation framework still unclear.
Freight and supply-chain disruption from Middle East conflict; inflationary pressure across operating costs; manufacturing costs drove ₹29.0 crore YoY increase in other operating costs (ex-freight).

qa_highlights.question: Why is US soft and how is FY28 $375m target achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the first two quarters will be soft with launches weighted to H2; five levers (controlled substances, new channels, new geographies/partnerships, launches, OTC) are expected to drive growth over the next 1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify revenue lost to freight-related supply delays in US?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify US loss; said the impact was elongated supply and that Ex-US shipment delays were temporary and expected to be caught up during the year.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt-free path?
qa_highlights.answer: Current net debt is about ₹1,420 crore excluding OneSource investment valued at about ₹320 crore; management expects broad neutrality in 2-3 years, noting ~₹300 crore debt reduction last year offset by rupee depreciation (INR82 to ~INR95-97/USD).

qa_highlights.question: Weighted cost of debt and debt mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Weighted cost of debt is about 7.6%, with major debt in India and the US; interest cost has fallen for 7-8 consecutive quarters. Management said CARE rating covers only a subset of loans.

qa_highlights.question: Controlled substance quota status?
qa_highlights.answer: Quota allocations happen twice a year based on past sales; controlled substances are about 5% of revenue; June cycle did not yield success, with a response expected in the next month.

qa_highlights.question: Product launches in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About 10 launches planned from now to 31 March 2027, with bulk of launches in H2 and profitability thresholds applied.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans for next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Spend of INR2.5-3.0 billion per year combining maintenance, R&D and hard capex; no greenfield plans under consideration.
